title: Former Director of Hardware Engineering at Meta Platforms Inc Believes Cooling Technology Startups Will Likely Be Acquired by Larger Industry Players
expert: Former Director of Hardware Engineering at Meta (interview 2026-08-07)
verdict: A former Meta hardware-engineering director says NVIDIA's A100 bare-die cooling attempt 'did not turn out well' with some customers and integrated chip-level cooling is five to seven years from shipping, so racks stay on ~30C liquid loops for now.

new_datapoints.text: NVIDIA A100 bare-die cooling attempt 'did not turn out well' with some customers; H100 bare-die effort complex with limitations
Integrated chip-level cooling five to six years (optimistic) / five to seven years (pessimistic) from shipping
Hyperscaler liquid-cooling converging on 30C loops; most operators avoid moving quickly to 18C
Cooling-startup acquisition outcomes ~$800 million to just under $2 billion vs $10B-$20B standalone unlikely
